unverified: No live director_message_received wake was observed, and none can be from a review worktree without driving a resident driver. I do not consider the author's coverage claim exact: the real-harness smoke test covers the BOOTSTRAP injection (it asserts the fixture inbox subject appears in the first model request through the pinned DSH binary) but not the wake path - no test emits a director_message_received event through boot() and asserts the steered digest. What IS covered for the wake is the pure projection plus eventCarriesSomething/ownEchoOnly on digest-shaped input. Risk is low (one call site, same function as bootstrap) but the claim 'the wiring is covered by the real-harness smoke test' is imprecise. What would close it: a boot() test against a stub State server that emits a director_message_received event, capturing the steered text and asserting digest-size/window; that needs no production wake.

The real page is ONE capture (91 matches, taken 2026-11-05). The superseded/short-excerpt rule never fires on it (0 threads with more than one message) and the omission path (items_omitted > 0) is synthetic only; both are asserted only by fixtures. A second capture after a threaded reply, and one after the inbox crosses 100 matches, would convert the two remaining synthetic claims into measurements.

The matched_total defect is proved from the server source, the existing contract test and two live reads of the same server, but was not measured end-to-end on a live inbox with more than 100 matches: the live match set is 91, which fits one request and yields correct numbers. The 101/120/250/500/600 rows come from a harness that reproduces the server's cursor semantics, not from production.

No live acknowledge was performed (I mutate no State): the ack fields are verified against acknowledge_director_message's signature, against real item shape from the live reads, and by mutant M3 reddening. Whether a director in practice acknowledges from the payload is a behavioural question this review did not observe.
Deployed server version vs this checkout was not compared beyond the two reads; if the deployment differs elsewhere in list_director_messages the honesty table would need re-running.

No pytest was run (the change is JavaScript only; the Python side is unchanged and was read, not executed). No repository test was run on the host or in the production container - only the JS suite with the pinned node in this worktree.

recommendation.land: as an improvement, after one fix
recommendation.must_fix: listProjectInbox must take matched_total from the FIRST page (after=0) instead of overwriting it on every page; has_more then follows from that total (already computed as matched_total > carried). Measured effect at 101 matches: stated total 1/has_more false -> 101/true. One line, no test rewrite, but the collector's test double should also stop returning store.length for every page - it currently makes the 600-match test assert 600 while production states 200.
recommendation.should_fix: (a) for a truncated scan, say that the carried items are the newest of the scanned slice, not the newest overall - 'newest 20 of 600 (scanned 500)' currently reads as the newest 20; (b) driver.md's 'read a whole body by message_id' should describe cursor paging (or the projection should keep delivery_seq), since no read action takes message_id; (c) the test comment's 87,720 raw-page figure measures 96,040.
recommendation.answer_to_the_review_question: The payload is genuinely bounded (11,921 chars against a 12,000 ceiling on the real page; 10,520 on the synthetic worst case) and the director does get the newest message first with a 176-char opening, body_chars and truncated=true, plus delivery_id and integer version so it can acknowledge from the payload it was handed, and the honest count holds while the match set fits one request (the current 91). It stops being honest at 101 matches, where the stated total becomes the last page's remainder and can say has_more false while 81 messages are invisible - a bounded payload that silently understates what it is not showing is the failure the change was meant to end, so fix it before the inbox gets there.
